Report for the fin ancial year ended March 31, 202 6.  
 
The AGM Notice and Annual Report  are also being uploaded on the website of the Company at  
https://www.religare.com/notices  and https://www.religare.com/annual -reports  respectively . 
 
Further, as per Section 108 of the Companies Act , 2013 read with Rule 20 of the Companies (Management

202 6. A person whose name is recorded in Register of Members and/ or in the register of beneficial owners

Wednesday , September  23, 202 6 (5.00 PM IST) .

1.  The Ministry of Corporate Affairs (“MCA”) , vide its General 
Circulars No. 20/2020 dated May 05, 2020 read with 
General Circular No. 14/2020 dated April 08, 2020 and 
General Circular No. 17/2020 dated April 13, 2020 and and 
subsequent circulars issued in this regard, latest being 
General Circular No. 03/2025 dated September 22, 2025 
(“MCA Circulars”)  and Securities and Exchange Board of 
India (“SEBI”)  vide its Circulars numbers SEBI/HO/CFD/
CMD1/CIR/P/2020/79 dated May 12, 2020 and SEBI/HO/
CFD/CFD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2024/133 dated October 03, 2024 
(“SEBI Circulars”)  (hereinafter collectively referred to as 
“the Circulars”) , have permitted the companies to conduct 
the Annual General Meeting through Video Conferencing 
/ Other Audio Visual Means (“VC” / “OAVM”) till further 
orders, without the physical presence of members at a 
common venue. Hence, in accordance with the Circulars, 
provisions of the Companies Act, 2013 (“the Act”) , and 
SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015 (“Listing Regulations”) , the 42nd Annual 
General Meeting (“AGM” / “Meeting”) of the Company is 
being held through VC /OAVM on Thursday, September 24, 
2026  at 03:00 P.M. (IST). The venue of the meeting shall be 
deemed to be at the Registered Office of the Company at 
First Floor, Office No. 101, 2E/23, Jhandewalan Extn., New 
Delhi – 110055.
2.  The attendance of the Members (members logins) 
attending the AGM through VC/OAVM will be counted for 
the purpose of reckoning the quorum under Section 103 
of the Act.
3.  In terms of the MCA Circulars, since the physical 
attendance of Members has been dispensed with, there 
is no requirement of appointment of proxies. Accordingly, 
the facility of appointment of proxies by Members 
under Section 105 of the Act will not be available for 
the AGM. However, the Body Corporate/Institutional/
Corporate members are entitled to appoint authorized 
representative to attend the AGM through VC/OAVM and 
participate thereat and cast their votes through e-voting.
4.  Since the AGM will be held through VC/OAVM facility, 
the attendance slip, proxy form and Route Map are not 
annexed to this Notice.
5.  Pursuant to the provisions of Section 113 of the Act, 
the Body Corporate/Institutional/Corporate members 
intending for their authorized representatives to attend 
the meeting and to vote at the AGM through e-voting 
facility are requested to send scanned certified true copy NOTES:
(PDF Format) of the latest Board Resolution/Authority 
Letter etc., together with attested specimen signature(s) 
of the duly authorised representative(s), to the Scrutinizer 
at email scrutinizer.maks@gmail.com  with a copy marked 
to einward.ris@kfintech.com  and evoting@kfintech.com . 
The scanned image of the above mentioned documents 
should be in the naming format “Religare Enterprises 
Limited, Event No. 10119” .
6.  Mr. Gurumurthy Ramanathan, whose office is liable to retire 
at the ensuing AGM, being eligible, seeks reappointment. 
The Nomination and Remuneration Committee and the 
Board of the Company, based on his performance are 
proposing his reappointment to the shareholders for 
consideration in the upcoming AGM.
  Relevant details in respect of Mr. Gurumurthy Ramanathan 
in terms of Regulation 36(3) of the Listing Regulations and 
Secretarial Standard on General Meetings (“SS-2”)  issued 
by the Institute of Company Secretaries of India (“ICSI”)  
are also annexed to this Notice.

Limited, Registrars and Share Transfer Agent (“RTA”) of the 
Company (hereinafter called “ KFintech ”), for conducting

8.  In line with the MCA Circulars, the Notice calling the AGM

directors, key managerial personnel, the Chairpersons

19.  Transmission:  Pursuant to Regulation 40 of SEBI Listing 
Regulations as amended from time to time, securities of 
listed companies can be transferred only in dematerialized 
form. Further, SEBI vide its Circular No. SEBI/HO/MIRSD/
MIRSD_RTAMB/P/ CIR/2022/8 dated January 25, 2022, 
has mandated listed companies to issue securities in 
dematerialized form while processing service request 
for issue of duplicate securities certificate / claim from 
unclaimed suspense account/ renewal/ exchange/ 
endorsement/ subdivision/ splitting/ consolidation/ 
transmission/ transposition of securities etc.
  Therefore, to avail various benefits of dematerialization 
and to eliminate the risks associated with physical 
shares, the shareholders are advised to dematerialise 
their physical shares. They are requested to get in touch 
with any Depository Participant having registration with 
SEBI to open a Demat account or alternatively, contact 
the nearest branch of KFintech to seek guidance on the 
Demat procedure. Members may also visit the website of 
depositories viz. NDSL: https://nsdl.co.in/faqs/faq.php  or 
CDSL: https://www.cdslindia.com/investors/open-demat.
html  for further understanding the demat procedure.
  Special Window for transfer and 
dematerialisation of physical securities
  Pursuant to SEBI Circular No. SEBI/ HO/38/13/11(2)2026-
MIRSD-POD/ I/3750/2026 dated January 30, 2026, 
the shareholders are hereby informed that a special 
window has been opened for a period of one year from February 05, 2026 to February 04, 2027, for Transfer and 
Dematerialisation of physical securities of the Company, 
which were sold/ purchased prior to April 01, 2019. The 
said special window shall also be available for such 
transfer requests which were submitted earlier and were 
rejected/returned/not attended to due to deficiency in 
the documents/process/or otherwise.
  Shareholders are encouraged to take advantage of this 
opportunity by furnishing the requisite documents, 
complete in all respects, as listed in the aforesaid SEBI 
circular to the REL’s Registrar and Share Transfer Agent 
(“RTA”) i.e. KFin Technologies Limited, Selenium Tower B, 
Plot 31-32, Gachibowli, Financial District, Nanakramguda 
Hyderabad, Telengana – 500032.
  Once all the documents are found in order by the 
RTA, securities so transferred shall be credited to the 
transferee only in demat mode and shall be under lock-
in for a period of one year from the date of registration 
of transfer. Such securities shall not be transferred/lien-
marked/pledged during the said lock-in period.
  For further details, shareholders may contact KFin 
Technologies Ltd. at the toll-free number 1-800-309-
4001 or email einward.ris@kfintech.com .

Non-convertible Redeemable Preference Shares (“Preference Shares”) of face value of I 10/-(Rupees 
Ten) each, voting rights triggered on the Preference 
Shares in terms of relevant provisions of the

filed a petition before the Hon’ble National Company 
Law Tribunal, New Delhi Bench (“NCLT) on June 14,

NCLT on September 29, 2021 directed ordering the 
status quo on the respondents to restrain them from 
exercising their voting power with the resolution until 
further order. Further, vide order dated December 
16, 2021, it was affirmed by Hon’ble NCLT that 
interim order will continue. The matter is currently 
sub-judice. Hence holders of said Preference Shares 
also will not be entitled to vote on the said resolution.

EXPLANATORY STATEMENT 
PURSUANT TO SECTION 102 OF THE COMPANIES ACT, 2013 AND OTHER APPLICABLE LAWS
ITEM NO. 4
To approve the re-designation of Mr. Arjun Lamba  
(DIN: 00124804), Whole-time Director (designated 
as Executive Director), as the Managing Director of 
the Company:
The Members are apprised that pursuant to the proposal 
received from promoter entities, the Company, based on the 
recommendation of Nomination and Remuneration Committee 
(NRC) on February 26, 2025 and approval of Board of Directors 
at their meeting held on the same date, had obtained approval 
of members, for the appointment of Mr. Arjun Lamba as Non-
Executive & Non-Independent Director of the Company, at 
their Extra-Ordinary General Meeting (‘EGM’) held on April 10, 
2025. The said appointment became effective from July 08, 
2025 being the date of receipt of approval from Reserve Bank 
of India (RBI).
Further, based on approval and recommendation of NRC 
and the Board of Directors, shareholders of the Company at 
their EGM held on May 05, 2026 approved the appointment 
of Mr. Arjun Lamba as Whole Time Director (designated as 
Executive Director) of the Company.
Proposal:
Since, Mr. Lamba is engaged in day-to-day affairs and 
management of the Company, NRC at its meeting held on 
August 12, 2026, recommended to Board, the re-designation 
of Mr. Arjun Lamba as Managing Director of the Company. The 
Board of Directors at their meeting held on the same date 
approved the re-designation of Mr. Arjun Lamba as Managing 
Director of the Company on the same terms and conditions; 
effective from August 12, 2026 for his remaining tenure and 
recommended the same for the approval of shareholders at 
their ensuing Annual General Meeting (‘AGM’).
The proposed re-designation is being made in view of 
the proposed assignment of overall responsibility for the 
management and affairs of the Company to Mr. Arjun Lamba 
in his capacity as Managing Director. The management 
believes that the proposed re-designation of Mr. Lamba 
will further strengthen the Board considering his vast and 
diversified experience.Members are further informed that the proposed re-designation 
does not involve any change in the tenure, remuneration or any 
other terms and conditions of appointment of Mr. Arjun Lamba 
as approved by the members through special resolution at the 
abovesaid EGM held on May 05, 2026 . Accordingly, the present 
proposal is only to modify the earlier resolution to the extent 
of changing the designation of Mr. Lamba from Whole-time 
Director (designated as Executive Director) to Managing 
Director. Accordingly, all other terms and conditions of his 
appointment, including tenure, remuneration and his status 
of being not liable to retire by rotation, shall remain unchanged.
Members are further apprised that Mr. Arjun Lamba has 
given his consent for the proposed re-designation and 
that the requisite documents/disclosures (viz. DIR-2, DIR-
8, MBP-1, Declaration confirming fulfillment of conditions 
prescribed in Part 1 of Sch. V of Companies Act, 2013, etc.) 
in relation to the proposed appointment in compliance with 
RBI (CIC) Directions 2025, Companies Act 2013, SEBI (Listing 
Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations 2015, 
(“SEBI LODR”), Director’s Appointment & Fit and Proper Policy, 
Director’s Remuneration Policy of the Company, KMPs & SMPs 
appointment and remuneration policy, Company’s internal 
policies and any other applicable law, have been received 
from him at the time of his appointment as Wholetime Director.
The Company has also received a duly signed declaration from 
Mr. Arjun Lamba confirming that he satisfies all conditions set 
out in Part-I of Schedule V and Section 196(3) of the Act.
Further, in opinion of the Board, Mr. Arjun Lamba fulfills the 
conditions specified in the Act read with the SEBI (Listing 
Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, 
relating to his appointment as Managing Director. He possesses 
the requisite skills, expertise and competencies identified by 
the Board for effective functioning of the Company. Details 
of director’s profile, qualification, experience, expertise and 
the information pursuant to regulation 36(3) of the Listing 
Regulations and Secretarial Standards on General Meetings 
are provided below.
Mr. Arjun Lamba has confirmed that he is neither disqualified 
from being appointed as a Director in terms of Section 164(2) 
of the Act, nor debarred from holding the office of director by 
virtue of any SEBI order or any other such authority.

BRIEF PROFILE MR. GURUMURTHY RAMANATHAN
Mr. Gurumurthy Ramanathan is a seasoned banking professional with 38 years of experience in India and overseas. His 
distinguished career encompasses leadership roles in corporate and institutional banking, wholesale banking, risk management, 
and governance across global and Indian institutions, including Bank of America, Standard Chartered, and the State Bank of India 
(SBI). During his tenure at RBL Bank, he oversaw assurance, technology, operations, and credit functions and headed Corporate 
and Institutional Banking during a transformational phase of the bank’s growth. In other roles, Mr. Gurumurthy managed strategic 
client relationships and contributed to organizational development.
Mr. Gurumurthy’s career achievements include building and leading transformation initiatives at RBL Bank after 2011, where he 
was instrumental in regulatory engagement and governance restructuring. He retired as Head of Governance at RBL Bank. Prior 
to this, at Standard Chartered, he established and headed the FI Strategic Coverage Group. 
His academic credentials include a B.A. from the University of Delhi and certification as an Associate of the Indian Institute of 
Bankers. Currently, he serves on the boards of Axis Capital Ltd., a subsidiary of Axis Bank, Simplex Infrastructures Ltd., Care Health 
Insurance Ltd., Religare Broking Ltd., and Religare Finvest Ltd. Known for his collaborative leadership style, Mr. Gurumurthy enjoys 
mentoring teams and advocates risk culture, integrated governance, and innovation in banking.
BRIEF PROFILE OF MR. ARJUN LAMBA
Mr. Arjun Lamba has served as the Executive Director of the Company since April 01, 2026. He is responsible for driving the 
Company’s strategic priorities, strengthening governance, supporting business transformation initiatives, and creating long-term 
value for all stakeholders. Prior to this, he served as a Non-Executive, Non-Independent Director of the Company. Mr. Lamba 
holds a BBA from École Les Roches, Switzerland. 
Mr. Lamba is also the founder of Guardian Advisors Private Limited, a SEBI-registered Portfolio Management Services (PMS) firm 
established in 2005. With over 23 years of experience in India’s capital markets, he has built deep expertise in equity investing and 
portfolio management. He has extensive experience in mergers and acquisitions and has played a critical role in the acquisitions 
and strategic transformation of both Eveready Industries and Religare Enterprises on behalf of the Burman family.
Mr. Lamba has also worked with Span Investments and Kotak Securities. He also serves as a Non-Executive, Non- Independent 
Director on the Board of Eveready Industries India Limited.

Building Wealth.  
Protecting Health.Contents
Financial security and healthcare protection are among the 
most enduring pillars of individual wellbeing and economic 
progress. At Religare Enterprises Limited (REL), these priorities 
define not only the businesses it operates, but also the purpose 
that guides its growth. Through focused financial services and 
health insurance businesses, the Group enables individuals, 
families and enterprises to build financial resilience while 
protecting what matters most.
FY26 marked an important inflection point in Religare’s 
evolution. A year defined by strengthened governance, 
renewed promoter conviction, enhanced leadership, fresh 
growth capital and significant regulatory milestones has 
positioned the Group to move beyond transformation towards 
disciplined, sustainable growth. Together, these developments 
have created a stronger institutional foundation from which 
each business can pursue its full potential with greater clarity 
and confidence.
The proposed demerger represents the next logical step in this 
evolution. Subject to the requisite regulatory and statutory 
approvals, the Group’s lending, broking and ancillary financial 
services businesses will be consolidated under Religare Finvest 
Limited to create an integrated financial services platform, 
while Religare Enterprises Limited will continue as a health insurance-focused holding company through its investment 
in Care Health Insurance Limited.
Each platform addresses a distinct yet complementary need.
The Financial Services platform will support entrepreneurship, 
home ownership, capital market participation and business 
expansion by improving access to specialised financial 
solutions. Care Health Insurance will continue to provide 
comprehensive health protection through a strong product 
portfolio, an expanding healthcare ecosystem and customer-
centric service capabilities.
Together, these businesses contribute to a common purpose: 
empowering customers to create financial security while 
safeguarding their health and wellbeing “Building Wealth. 
Protecting Health” is therefore more than the theme of this 
Annual Report. It reflects the strategic identity Religare is 
building: two focused platforms, each with a clear purpose, 
dedicated governance and disciplined capital allocation, 
united by a commitment to customer-centricity, operational 
excellence and long-term value creation.02

Religare Enterprises Limited is building a focused platform around two of India’s 
most enduring structural opportunities: financial services and health insurance. 
As a Core Investment Company (CIC) registered with the Reserve Bank of India, 
REL provides strategic direction, governance oversight and long-term capital 
stewardship across businesses that help individuals, entrepreneurs and  
enterprises build financial resilience and create long-term value.
The Group’s businesses span MSME lending, affordable housing 
finance, retail and institutional broking, and health insurance, 
serving customers across every stage of their financial and 
healthcare journeys. Together, these businesses are united 
by a common philosophy: delivering responsible, customer-
centric solutions supported by sound governance, disciplined 
execution and prudent risk management.
FY26 marked a defining year in the Company’s evolution. 
Strengthened leadership, enhanced governance, renewed 
promoter commitment, successful capital mobilisation 
and the proposed demerger have collectively reinforced 
Religare’s institutional strength and strategic direction. These 
developments position each business to pursue its own 
growth agenda with greater focus, operational agility and 
capital discipline while creating long-term value for customers, 
shareholders and other stakeholders.Strong Promoter Commitment
The Burman Group’s continued support during FY26 
reflects its long-term conviction in Religare’s future. 
Through its participation in the Company’s growth 
capital initiatives and by increasing its shareholding 
throughout the year, the promoter group has 
demonstrated confidence not only in the Company’s 
businesses but also in its governance framework, 
strategic direction and long-term growth potential. 
This commitment further strengthens Religare’s 
institutional foundation as it enters its next phase of 
focused growth.
Built Around What Matters Most  
At the heart of Religare’s philosophy lies a simple belief: 
meaningful progress begins with financial confidence and 
healthcare security.
Whether enabling businesses and individuals to access 
capital, helping families realise the dream of home ownership, 
supporting investors in capital markets or protecting 
individuals through comprehensive health insurance, every business within the Group exists to solve real-world needs 
with practical, trusted and customer-centric solutions.
As the Group evolves, this commitment remains unchanged 
to build enduring businesses that create sustainable value for 
customers, shareholders, employees and the communities the 
Group serves.Who We Are Our Values

an integrated financial services platform bringing together the 
Group’s lending, affordable housing finance, broking and related 
financial services businesses. Religare Enterprises Limited will 
continue as a health insurance-focused holding company through 
its investment in Care Health Insurance Limited.
The proposed structure enables each platform to pursue its 
own strategic priorities with greater agility, optimise capital 
deployment, strengthen accountability and unlock value 
aligned to the unique dynamics of its respective sector, while 
continuing to uphold the shared principles of governance, 
customer focus and responsible growth.
Integrated Financial Services Platform
The integrated Financial Services platform will bring together 
specialised businesses serving individuals, entrepreneurs and 
enterprises through comprehensive financial solutions across 
lending, housing finance and capital markets.
The platform will comprise:
• Religare Finvest Limited:  Providing MSME lending solutions 
that enable businesses to access working capital and 
growth finance.
• Religare Housing Development Finance Corporation 
Limited: Delivering affordable housing finance 
that supports home ownership across urban and 
emerging markets.
• Religare Broking Limited:  Enabling retail and institutional 
investors to participate confidently in India’s growing 
capital markets through technology-enabled 
investment solutions.Building Wealth Unlocking Value Through  
Greater Strategic Focus
During FY26, the Boards of Religare 
Enterprises Limited and Religare 
Finvest Limited approved a Scheme 
of Arrangement for the demerger, 
transfer and vesting of the financial 
services business from Religare 
Enterprises Limited to Religare Finvest 
Limited. Subject to requisite regulatory 
and statutory approvals, the Scheme 
will result in two separately listed, 
strategically focused businesses.
The proposed restructuring  
reflects the Group’s conviction 
that businesses with dedicated

and independent capital allocation 
are better positioned to respond 
to market opportunities, accelerate 
growth and create sustainable long-

Focused PlatformsTogether, these businesses expand access to credit, home

financial resilience while supporting entrepreneurship and 
economic development.
Protecting Health
Health Insurance Platform
Care Health Insurance will continue to serve as the Group’s health insurance 
platform, providing comprehensive health protection solutions for individuals, 
families and corporates.
Supported by strong underwriting expertise, digital innovation and as India’s second-
largest standalone health insurer, Care Health Insurance continues to provide access 
to quality healthcare while helping customers protect themselves from the financial 
impact of medical uncertainty.
As one of India’s leading standalone health insurers, the business remains committed 
to delivering responsive service, innovative products and long-term customer value, 
reinforcing Religare’s broader purpose of enabling healthier, more secure lives.Why the Demerger?
• Streamlining businesses
• Separate listing of financial 
services business
• Focused management attention
• Stronger risk management 
and compliance
Religare Enterprises Limited and Religare Finvest Limited had applied 
to the Reserve Bank of India(“RBI”)  for its no-objection/prior approval. 
By letters dated August 6, 2026 and August 7, 2026, addressed to 
Religare Enterprises Limited and Religare Finvest Limited , respectively, 
the RBI communicated that, following examination of the applications, 
the request could not be acceded to. REL and RFL are evaluating the 
communications and remain engaged with the RBI to provide any 
further clarifications that may be required.Together, these two focused pillars represent REL’s long-term vision—  
creating a stronger, more focused enterprise that combines  
financial confidence with healthcare security.

Message from the   
Chairperson
India's credit markets are experiencing a fundamental shift 
in composition and delivery. While traditional banking 
continues to deploy substantial capital, non-bank lending 
platforms are capturing growing market share and emerging as 
indispensable channels for credit access. Assets held by non-
banking financial companies have expanded significantly since 
the start of this decade, with retail borrowers now representing 
a material and growing portion of these portfolios. The sector 
has navigated regulatory transitions successfully, with housing 
finance demonstrating notable recovery in asset quality 
and digital lending platforms showing renewed momentum. 
Demand for purpose-built credit solutions, whether for 
home purchase, SMEs business growth, or personal needs; 
they continue to expand faster than traditional channels can 
serve. This opportunity is being amplified by automation, 
data analytics, and emerging technologies that enable faster 
underwriting, better risk assessment, and personalised 
customer experiences.
India's financial markets have also evolved from a capital 
formation story into one of institutional maturity and quality. 
The quantum of capital mobilisation through securities 
markets has expanded substantially, reflecting both domestic 
prosperity and global recognition of Indian market governance 
standards. What distinguishes current-cycle growth is the 
composition of participants such as domestic institutional 
investors have become the primary decision-makers 
rather than price-takers following overseas sentiment. The 
companies accessing capital markets today exhibit stronger 
financial discipline and governance than in previous periods, 
indicating a natural selection towards quality. India's standing 
as a credible, transparent, and increasingly autonomous 
capital destination continues to strengthen.Within this environment of structural credit expansion and 
market maturation, Religare is distinctly positioned to capture 
these opportunities.
This year's annual report theme reflects what we do: “Building 
Wealth, Protecting Health”. Our financial services businesses, 
Religare Finvest, Religare Housing Development Finance, and 
Religare Broking help customers build wealth at every stage of 
life. Care Health Insurance protects that wealth by shielding 
families from financial hardship when illness strikes. Together, 
these two segments tell one story: a Group that helps people 
build what matters, and protects what they have built.
We successfully made a preferential issue of I 1,500 Crore in 
which the Burman Group, our new promoters, contributed half 
of this amount, a clear signal of their conviction in Religare's 
direction and future success.  This is growth capital. It 
strengthens our balance sheet and enables  funds expansion. 
It supports the technology investment we need to scale. 
Care Health Insurance received additional capital to sustain 
its growth and solvency. Our wealth-building businesses are 
equally well capitalised. Each now has the foundation it needs 
to grow responsibly.
The Board appointed additional directors this year, bringing 
fresh experience in banking, technology, and financial 
services. Mr. Arjun Lamba has been designated Managing 
Director, a reflection of our confidence in his ability to lead 
this next chapter.
We are rebuilding our senior leadership across both segments. 
Care Health Insurance, Religare Finvest, Religare Housing 
Development Finance, and Religare Broking each now have new 
leadership at the helm. Fresh appointments across finance, 
legal, HR, and compliance at the Group level complete this 
coordinated rebuild. Every business is ready to scale to its 
next level.I extend my gratitude to all our shareholders. Thank you for your 
unwavering trust, guidance and confidence throughout this 
journey. Your collective support has enabled us to strengthen 
our foundations, reaffirm the value of disciplined execution 
and position the Group for its next phase of growth. As we 
enter this new chapter, we remain committed to responsible 
growth, sound governance, consistent execution and creating 
sustainable long-term value while continuing to earn your trust 
every step of the way.
I am also thankful to my colleague directors on the Board of 
the Company for their active guidance. We are thankful to all 
our stakeholders, including bankers, regulatory, other central 
and state authorities. I am also thankful to all our colleagues 
and employees for their sincerity and hard work. 
Thank you my dear shareholders for your continued confidence 
in the Company.
With best regards,
Rajender Mohan Malla

Message from the  
Managing Director
Dear Shareholders,
FY26 has been a defining year for Religare. It was 
a year of restoring confidence, strengthening our 
foundations and preparing each of our businesses for 
disciplined, long-term growth. Throughout the year, 
our focus remained clear: reinforce governance, build 
the right leadership, allocate capital responsibly and 
create the conditions for consistent execution.
Several important milestones marked this journey. The 
Reserve Bank of India lifted the Corrective Action Plan (CAP) 
applicable to our MSME lending business, legacy fraud-related 
tags were removed, and our reconstituted management 
structure received the necessary regulatory approvals. 
These developments are more than regulatory outcomes. 
They reflect the progress we have made in strengthening 
our governance, improving risk management and rebuilding 
institutional credibility.
A significant step during the year was the successful capital 
raise of  I1,500 Crore. Half of this capital was contributed by 
our promoters, the Burman Group reaffirming their long-term 
commitment to Religare. Capital, however, delivers value only 
when deployed with discipline. Accordingly, we have allocated 
resources across our businesses based on their respective 
growth requirements while preserving adequate flexibility for 
future opportunities. Religare Finvest also remains debt-free 
with a strong capital position, providing it with the financial 
strength to pursue its next phase of growth responsibly.
Strong institutions are built by capable people. During FY26, we 
strengthened leadership across the Group with experienced 
professionals across our businesses and corporate functions. 
New leadership appointments in Religare Finvest, Religare 
Housing Development Finance Corporation, Religare Broking 
and Group functions, along with leadership transitions within 
Care Health Insurance, have brought together teams with 
proven execution capabilities and deep domain expertise. 
Equally important, we strengthened our governance 
architecture through key appointments in Board, finance and 
compliance, reinforcing our commitment to transparency, 
accountability and sound decision-making.
The Board approved the demerger of our financial services 
business from our health insurance business, guided by three 
clear reasons. 
First, management focus:  each vertical will have a dedicated 
leadership and governance, without the distraction of running 
a diversified conglomerate spanning fundamentally different 
regulatory and capital requirements. Second, shareholder flexibility:  our shareholders will gain the 
freedom to hold exposure to both segments separately. 
Third, accountability:  employees across both segments will be 
measured on, and rewarded for, the performance of their own 
business, rather than a blended outcome.
Across our businesses, the year reflected encouraging 
operational progress.
Our health insurance platform, Care Health Insurance, 
continued to reinforce its leadership position during FY26, 
delivering another year of strong operational and financial 
performance. Gross Written Premium grew 24% y-o-y to  
I11,417 Crore when computed without 1/n basis, while the 
retail health portfolio expanded by 34%, reflecting continued 
strength in its core business. The business reported a Profit 
Before Tax of I 519 Crore basis Ind AS accounting and a Return 
on Average Equity of 19.4% on PBT basis, while its credit 
rating was upgraded to the AA family. Care also maintained a 
healthy solvency ratio of 1.68 and a claim settlement ratio of 
more than 97%, supported by a network of about over 22,040 
hospital tie-ups. Continued investments in digital capabilities, 
customer experience and disciplined underwriting have further 
strengthened the business, positioning it to create sustained 
value in India's growing health insurance market.
Religare Finvest completed an important phase in its 
transformation during FY26. The business reported a profit of  
I139 Crore, maintained a 98% collection efficiency, remained 
debt-free, and closed the year with a Capital Adequacy Ratio 
of 261% and a Net Worth of I 900 Crore. The removal of the 
RBI's Corrective Action Plan, together with the resolution of 
legacy regulatory matters, marked a significant milestone in 
restoring the business to normal operations. Supported by 
surplus liquidity of over  I591 Crore, our focus remains on 
strengthening technology, credit processes, risk management 
and distribution capabilities to build a resilient platform for 
the future.Religare Housing Finance continued to build a stable foundation 
in the affordable housing finance segment through prudent 
underwriting and disciplined growth. The business managed 
Assets Under Management (AUM) of  I243 Crore, maintained 
a 101% collection efficiency and a Capital Adequacy Ratio 
of 130%, while retaining investment-grade ratings from both 
ICRA and CARE Ratings. With operations spanning 15 branches 
across eight states, the business continues to expand its 
presence in underserved markets where long-term demand 
for affordable housing remains strong.
Religare Broking continued to strengthen its franchise in a 
competitive market environment, serving over one million 
registered clients, including 2.5 Lakh active customers. The 
business reported total income of I 373 Crore and a Profit After 
Tax of  I23 Crore, with profitability strengthening significantly 
during the final quarter of the year. The Dynami trading 
platform continued to deepen digital engagement, supported 
by a diversified revenue base and continued investments in 
technology and customer experience, the business remains 
well positioned to participate in India's expanding retail 
investing ecosystem.
The progress achieved this year has been made possible by 
the trust and commitment of many stakeholders. I would like 
to thank our Board for its stewardship, our business partners 
for their continued confidence, our shareholders for their 
unwavering support and, above all, our employees whose 
resilience, professionalism and commitment have driven 
this transformation.
We remain committed to create enduring value  
through responsible growth, disciplined execution and an 
unwavering focus on the interests of all our stakeholders.
Yours sincerely,
Arjun Lamba  
Managing Director

Governance
Guiding Growth With  
Thoughtful Leadership
Board of Directors
Mr. Arjun Lamba is serving as Managing Director of Religare 
Enterprises Limited. He is responsible for driving the 
Company’s strategic priorities, strengthening governance, 
supporting business transformation initiatives, and creating 
long-term value for all stakeholders. Prior to this, he served as 
a Non-Executive, Non-Independent Director on the Board of 
Religare Enterprises Limited. Mr. Lamba holds a BBA from École 
Les Roches, Switzerland.
Mr. Lamba is also the founder of Guardian Advisors Private 
Limited, a SEBI-registered Portfolio Management Services 
(PMS) firm established in 2005. With over 23 years of experience in India’s capital markets, he has built deep expertise in 
equity investing and portfolio management. He has extensive 
experience in mergers and acquisitions and has played a 
critical role in the  acquisitions and strategic transformation 
of both Eveready Industries and Religare Enterprises on behalf

Directors' Report
To,
The Members,
Religare Enterprises Limited
Your Directors are pleased to present this 42nd Annual Report 
on the business and operations of the Company together with 
Audited Financial Statements for the financial year ended 
March 31, 2026.
STATE OF AFFAIRS OF THE COMPANY
The financial year 2025-26 marked a significant milestone in 
the Company’s journey, with the transition to a promoter–
led ownership structure, strengthening of the Board and 
leadership team, strategic capital augmentation initiatives and 
stakeholder value creation.
A significant milestone for the Company was the Burman 
Group being designated as the promoters of the Company 
following the completion of the Open Offer in February 2025. 
The induction of the new promoters marked the beginning 
of a new era in the Company’s journey, bringing long term 
strategic ownership, enhanced governance framework, capital 
commitment and renewed focus.
In line with the change in ownership and strategic direction, 
the Company undertook significant measures to strengthen 
its Board and leadership architecture. In February 2025, 
the Board was further reinforced through the induction of 
two independent directors and during the year, three non-
independent directors who bring expertise across financial 
services, insurance, strategy, governance and business 
transformation were also inducted. The strengthened 
leadership is expected to support improved execution 
capabilities, sharper strategic focus and sustained value 
creation across the Company’s businesses.
During the year, the Company raised ` 1,50,000 Lakhs by way 
of a preferential issue of warrants convertible into equity 
shares. This initiative is aimed at supporting the future growth 
trajectory of the Company and strengthen its financial position 
to enable strategic investment across subsidiaries.
As part of the Company’s long-term strategic roadmap, 
the Board of REL approved a Scheme of Arrangement on 
February 14, 2026 for the demerger of its Financial Services 
business. The proposed restructuring is aimed at creating two focused and independently managed entities thereby 
simplifying the group structure, enhancing operational focus 
and facilitating efficient capital allocation and value creation 
for all stakeholders.
On the operational front, the Company’s subsidiaries 
continued to demonstrate growth.
• Care Health Insurance Limited (CHIL), the Company’s 
Standalone Health Insurance arm, maintained its position as 
the second largest Standalone Health Insurance Company 
(SAHI) and continued to be the fastest growing in its 
segment. CHIL recorded a Gross- Written Premium (GWP) 
of ` 10,41,6451 Lakhs for FY26.
• Religare Broking Limited (RBL), the Company's broking arm, 
delivered a resilient performance despite a challenging 
operating environment for the broking industry. On a 
consolidated basis, RBL and its subsidiaries reported 
revenue of ` 37,336.08 Lakh for FY26.
• Religare Finvest Limited (RFL), having resolved its legacy 
issues, has discharged all outstanding obligations to its 
lenders and remains debt-free. The Hon’ble High Court 
of Delhi on July 22, 2025 ordered to remove “fraud” 
classification tag assigned by certain banks. The Reserve 
Bank of India (RBI) removed the Corrective Action Plan 
(CAP), effective July 23, 2025, thereby paving the way for the 
recommencement of business operations. RFL is entering 
a new phase of its journey with renewed strategic direction 
focused on building a resilient, technology- enabled 
portfolio, which support its future growth strategy.
• Religare Housing Development Finance Corporation Limited 
(RHDFCL), continues to focus on its core retail lending 
business to self-employed and informal segments while 
reducing exposure to non-core and non-retail segments. 
This strategy has resulted in a more granular and stable 
portfolio profile. The Company remains focused on 
expanding its affordable housing portfolio while maintaining 
prudent credit and risk management standards.
The aforesaid developments collectively represent important 
strategic milestones for the Company. With a committed 
promoter group, strengthened governance and leadership 
structure in place, the Company is well positioned to enhance 
operational performance, pursue new growth opportunities 
and create sustainable long term value for all stakeholders.FINANCIAL RESULTS AND BUSINESS OPERATIONS

  The Board of Directors of Religare Enterprises Limited

Demerged Undertaking (as defined in the Scheme), 
being the financial services business of the Company, 
comprising of lending activities, broking activities, 
investment activities and ancillary and support services, 
from REL into RFL on a going concern basis and various 
other matters consequent and incidental thereto or 
integrally connected thereto. The Remaining Business 
of REL, including its insurance business comprising of its 
investment in Care Health Insurance Limited will continue 
to be held by REL.
  The proposed demerger is designed to achieve four 
key objectives:
• Streamlining businesses:  Segregation of financial 
services from insurance to create independent, 
focused entities that can attract different investor 
profiles suited to each sector.
• Listing financial services business:  Separate listing 
of RFL to unlock value for shareholders and enable 
pursuit of distinct growth opportunities.
• Focused management attention:  Enable mapping of 
employee performance and rewards to respective 
business outcomes, and facilitate attraction and 
retention of sector-specific talent and resources.
• Risk management and compliance:  Implement risk 
management policies and internal compliance frameworks tailored to each business, improving 
monitoring and control.
  Further, as contemplated in the Scheme, the Scheme is 
in the interest of all stakeholders of REL and RFL.
  As a consideration for the proposed transfer, RFL will issue 
1 (one) fully paid up equity share having a face value of 
` 10 (Rupees Ten only) each for 1 (one) fully paid up equity 
share of `  10 (Rupees Ten only) each of the Company. 
Upon the Scheme becoming effective and issue of the 
said consideration, the equity shares of RFL will be listed 
on BSE Limited (“BSE”) and National Stock Exchange of 
India Limited (“NSE”).
  The Scheme is inter alia subject to receipt of the 
approvals of shareholders and creditors of REL and RFL, 
respectively, Securities and Exchange Board of India, 
Reserve Bank of India (“RBI”), jurisdictional National 
Company Law Tribunal, and other regulatory authorities, 
as may be applicable.
• In connection with the Scheme, the Company had 
made applications to the NSE and BSE seeking its 
no-objection / prior approval / observation letter to 
the Scheme. The Company has received observation 
letters dated July 07, 2026, with ‘no objection’ from NSE 
and ‘no adverse observations’ from BSE, respectively.
• Further, REL and RFL had made applications to the 
RBI seeking its no-objection/ prior approval. The RBI, 
vide its letter dated August 6, 2026, issued to REL, has 
conveyed that the said application has been examined 
and that the request could not be acceded to. A similar 
communication dated August 7, 2026, has also been 
received by RFL. REL and RFL are evaluating the said 
communications and engaging with the RBI to provide 
such further clarifications as may be required by the 
RBI in this regard.
  The relevant documents as required under applicable 
law, are hosted on the website of the Company  
at https://www.religare.com/scheme-of-arrangement .

4.  Revival of Religare Finvest Limited
• Removal of Fraud Tag
During the previous financial year, on July 22, 2025, 
the Hon’ble Delhi High Court quashed the fraud 
classification by certain lenders against RFL and 
directed the lenders to take necessary steps for 
removal of such classification from RFL’s records 
maintained with the Central Fraud Registry (CFR).
All lenders confirmed the removal of RFL’s fraud 
classification from the CFR database.
• Removal of Corrective Action Plan by RBI
RBI, vide its letter dated January 18, 2018, had advised 
RFL to adhere to the Corrective Action Plan (CAP), 
which, inter alia, imposed restrictions on the extension of credit/investment, except in specified permitted 
categories and prohibited the declaration of dividends. 
These restrictions were imposed in the context of 
instances of financial mismanagement under the 
erstwhile promoters, including the diversion of funds 
through Corporate Loan Book (CLB) transactions and 
other non-core investments.
Over the years, RFL submitted various representations 
and communications to RBI seeking withdrawal of the 
CAP restrictions. Pursuant to its assessment of RFL’s 
compliance with the applicable requirements, RBI vide 
its letter dated July 23, 2025, informed RFL that the CAP 
conditions and related restrictions had been withdrawn. 
RBI also acknowledged the measures undertaken by 
RFL, including changes in its management and Board 
of Directors and accordingly permitted withdrawal of 
the restrictions with immediate effect.
• Strategic Roadmap for RFL
Following the removal of the regulatory restrictions, 
RFL has focused on strengthening its institutional 
and operational framework and establishing the 
necessary foundations for the measured revival of its 
lending operations.
During the year, RFL placed significant emphasis on 
strengthening Board oversight, enhancing its senior 
management team, reinforcing governance and 
further developing its risk management and internal 
control system. These measures are aimed at ensuring 
that RFL’s operations remain aligned with regulatory 
requirements and prudent industry practices.
Going forward, RFL intends to progressively build a 
scalable and diversified lending franchise, with a focus 
on disciplined underwriting, prudent risk management 
and effective portfolio monitoring. RFL also proposes 
to leverage technology and digital capabilities to 
improve operational efficiency, enhance credit 
decision-making and strengthen portfolio monitoring 
across the lending lifecycle.
RFL’s strategy will remain focused on sustainable and 
responsible growth, supported with sound governance, 
robust risk management and financial discipline. RFL 
will continue to invest in its people, technology and 
processes to strengthen its operating capabilities 
and position the business for measured growth while 
creating value for its customers, shareholders and all 
other stakeholders.
With strengthened governance structures, an 
experienced leadership team and a clearly defined 
strategic roadmap, RFL is well positioned to progressively participate in the evolving financial 
services landscape.
5.  Composite Scheme of Arrangement
  In FY 2022-23, Religare Broking Limited (“RBL” or “the 
Transferor Company”), a wholly owned subsidiary of the 
Company, and Religare Digital Solutions Limited (“RDSL” 
or “the Transferee Company”), wholly owned subsidiary of 
RBL, approved a Scheme of Arrangement (“the Scheme”) 
under section 230-232 of the Companies Act, 2013. The 
Scheme inter alia provides for transfer of E-Governance 
Undertaking of the Transferor Company to the Transferee 
Company on a “slump sale” basis, as a going concern 
with the appointed date for the Scheme being April 01, 
2022 in accordance with provisions of the Scheme. The 
Hon’ble NCLT vide order dated June 13, 2025, approved 
the Scheme of Arrangement between RBL and RDSL, with 
effect from the Appointed Date, i.e., April 1, 2022, subject 
to certain conditions as outlined in the Order. Upon filing 
of the certified copy of the Order with the Registrar of 
Companies on August 19, 2025, the Scheme became 
effective in accordance with its terms. Consequently, 
during the current financial year, the E-Governance 
Business stands transferred to RDSL.

Garnishee, which is being contested / challenged. Further, 
the Company has also filed a criminal complaint before the 
Economic Offences Wing, Delhi Police for various offences 
under the Indian Penal Code, 1860 w.r.t transactions relating 
to issuance and redemption of said Preference Shares.
Further, due to non-payment of dividend by the Company 
continuously for two years on 2016 Preference Shares, voting 
rights triggered on these Preference Shares in terms of relevant 
provisions of the Act. The Company has also not paid dividend 
on 2008 Preference Shares but the Company has a letter dated 
August 20, 2012 from then holder of these 2008 Preference 
shares irrevocably and unconditionally waiving off the voting 
rights on 2008 Preference Shares. The Company has not 
redeemed aforesaid 2016 Preference Shares with redemption 
value amounting `  4,212.75 Lakhs due for redemption on 
August 30, 2021 and which is outstanding as of March 31, 2026.
The Company has filed the petition before the Hon’ble National 
Company Law Tribunal, New Delhi Bench seeking rectification 
of Register of Members of the Company by cancellation of 2016 Preference Shares and any other appropriate reliefs, 
including interim relief with respect to freezing of voting rights 
and dividend rights attached to the said 2016 Preference 
Shares. The Hon’ble NCLT on September 29, 2021 directed 
ordering the status quo on the respondents to restrain them 
from exercising their voting power with the resolution until the 
further order. Further, vide order dated December 16, 2021, 
it was affirmed by Hon’ble Tribunal that interim order will 
continue. The matter is sub-judice.
The Company on prudent basis had created a provision 
of ` 2,941.67 Lakhs towards the potential interest liability 
from the redemption date till March 31, 2023 on aforesaid 
Preference Shares. However, based on its re-assessment of 
the facts of the matter and as advised by the legal experts 
as at March 31, 2023, the Company is of the view that there 
will be no contractual or legal obligation on the Company to 
pay any compensation/interest in lieu of the unredeemed 
Preference Shares or on its redemption value irrespective 
of what may be the final outcome of the matters regarding 
the payment of total redemption value of `  8,403.03 Lakhs 
which are presently sub-judice. Accordingly, the provision 
created towards contingency of `  2,941.67 Lakhs was reversed 
during the year ended March 31, 2023. However, the provision 
towards the redemption value has been continued on prudent 
/ conservative basis.

CAPITAL REQUIREMENTS
Your Company is registered with the RBI as a Core Investment 
Company (CIC) vide Certificate No. N-14.03222 dated June 03, 
2014, and is classified as a NBFC – Middle Layer in accordance 
with the RBI Scale Based Regulatory Framework. As a CIC, your 
Company is primarily engaged in the business of investment in 
shares of and lending to its group companies holding not less 
than 90% of its net assets in the form of investment in equity 
shares, preference shares, bonds, debentures, debt or loans 
in group companies.

 31
Corporate Overview Financial Statements Statutory Reports Annual Report 2025-2026
=== page 38 ===
Being a CIC, the requirement of capital adequacy is not 
in the form of Capital to Risk Weighted Assets (CRAR) like 
conventional credit and investment companies. The Company 
is required to –
a.  maintain minimum Adjusted Net Worth of 30% of its 
aggregate risk weighted assets on balance sheet and risk 
adjusted value of off-balance sheet items as on the date 
of the last audited balance sheet as at the end of the 
financial year; and
b.  restrict the outside liabilities up to 2.5 times of its 
Adjusted Net Worth as on the date of the last audited 
balance sheet as at the end of the financial year.
The Company is in compliance with the abovementioned 
requirements as on March 31, 2026.
Further, in compliance with the RBI (Core Investment 
Companies) Directions, 2025 read with (Non-Banking Financial 
Companies – Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy) Directors, 
2025, as amended the Company conducted an Internal Capital 
Adequacy Assessment (ICAAP) based on its financial position 
as on March 31, 2026 basis the Company’s ICAAP policy. It 
was observed that the Company was adequately capitalized 
to cover for all material risks.

INTERNAL CAPITAL ADEQUACY ASSESSMENT 
PROCESS (“ICAAP”)
In compliance with the RBI (Core Investment Companies) 
Directions, 2025 read with RBI (Non-Banking Financial 
Companies – Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy) 
Directions, 2025 as amended, the Company being a NBFC 
Middle Layer is required to make a thorough internal 
assessment of the need for capital, commensurate with the 
risks in their business, on similar lines as ICAAP prescribed for 
commercial banks under Pillar 2 under RBI (Commercial Bank 
– Prudential Norms on Capital Adequacy) Direction, 2025, as 
amended in line with the Company’s comprehensive board – 
approved ICAAP Policy.
The objective of ICAAP is to assess on an ongoing basis 
the adequacy of capital so as to ensure availability of 
capital considering all risks in business so as to enable 
better assessment, monitoring and management of risks as 
well as efficient capital management and capital planning 
commensurate with the business of the Company and risks 
it is exposed to.
The Company conducted an ICAAP as per the ICAAP Policy, the 
ICAAP indicated that the Company is adequately capitalized 
to cover for all the material risks including in stress scenarios.COMPLIANCE POLICY

As required under the Regulation 34 of SEBI LODR Regulations

AS-110 “Consolidated Financial Statements” issued by the

MCA. The audited consolidated financial statements together 
with Auditor’s Report form part of the Annual Report.
Though, the Company holds 100% equity share capital in 
Religare Capital Markets Limited (“RCML”), however in the 
present scenario controlling through voting rights of RCML is not 
there with the Company. Beside this, the tripartite agreement 
entered into, in financial year 2011-12, between REL, RCML and 
RHC Holding Private Limited (“RHCHPL”), for providing financial 
support to RCML by RHCHPL (by subscribing Preference 
Shares of RCML), severe long term restrictions and significant 
restrictive covenants on major decision making at RCML were 
imposed by the holder of preference shares. Accordingly, 
in view of the above, the financial statements of RCML and 
its subsidiaries have been excluded from the consolidated 
financial statements of the Company w.e.f. October 01, 2011, 
in accordance with applicable accounting standards. The 
Company has already provided fully for the entire investment 
made by it in RCML in previous years.
The consolidated financial statements presented by your 
Company, including financial information of all its subsidiaries, 
excluding RCML and RCML’s subsidiaries, have been duly 
audited by the Statutory Auditors and the same is published

RISK MANAGEMENT
Risk Governance is an essential aspect of the strategy 
of the Company intended at identification, assessment 
and mitigation of the potential risks that could affect the 
Company’s operations, financial performance, sustainability 
and reputation. The Board of Directors of the Company are 
responsible for ensuring oversight of the risk management 
policies & procedures and has constituted a Group Risk 
Management Committee (GRMC), which is ultimately 
responsible to frame, implement, monitor and periodically 
review the effectiveness of the risk management plan and make 
appropriate modifications as and when necessary. GRMC’s 
role has been aligned to requirements of the Companies Act, 
2013, SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015, RBI Master Directions for Core Investment 
Companies and other applicable regulatory requirements. 
Process has been laid down to periodically apprise the GRMC 
about prevalent risks and corrective plans adopted by the 
respective group entities to mitigate the identified risks.
The Company is registered as a Core Investment Company. 
As an investment holding company, the management function 
includes oversight of risk function prevalent to the Company 
and its key operating subsidiaries. The Company has a 
comprehensive Risk Management framework and overarching 
Risk Management Policy, which has been adopted by each of 
the key operating subsidiaries while formulating their Risk 
Management Policy. Key risks applicable to the Company are 
identified in the Risk Management Policy of the Company. Risk 
Management Policy is aimed at identification, assessment, 
mitigation, monitoring and reporting of identifiable risks and 
documenting of each identified risk along with the mitigation 
plan. Respective functional head and/or risk management 
department of key operating subsidiaries are responsible 
for implementation of the Risk Management system and 
maintenance of record of risk and mitigation plan in Risk & 
Control Matrix (RCMs) for their respective functional areas, 
which are updated and tested periodically. Therefore, the 
risk governance and framework defines the risk management 
approach including risk identification, documentation, testing 
and reporting on a periodical basis. The framework has 
different risk parameters, which help in identification of risks 
and their classification as High, Medium and Low categories 
based on likelihood, impact and velocity in various risk types 
such as operational, financial, compliance and reputation risk. 
Qualitative and quantitative assessment is done to determine the likelihood and impact of identified risks, which are ultimately 
plotted on a matrix based on severity and probability.
Further, the company has developed a subsidiary risk limit 
framework, constituting prudential limits and associated risk 
tolerance limits of subsidiaries, which is a robust framework 
for governance of subsidiaries especially in terms of risk 
management parameters and corresponding threshold to 
be monitored by the Company in a periodic manner. This 
subsidiary risk limits framework aligns with the regulatory 
and business requirements to monitor major risk thresholds 
emanating from key industry and regulatory risk at each 
subsidiary level. Framework is structured to align with REL’s 
business objectives and to adapt to the dynamic external 
environment, technological advancements and evolving 
global standards and best practices. It aims to safeguard 
the continuity of operations and protect the interests of all 
stakeholders, customers, business partners, outsourced 
service providers, employees and regulators for the holding 
company as well as the subsidiaries.
Reviews and reporting of risk environment and performance 
is conducted on a quarterly basis. The testing and evaluation 
of control environment around Risk Management is integrated 
and aligned with the quarterly internal audit process. The 
GRMC of the Company and respective Risk Management 
Committee/Board of Directors of its key operating subsidiaries 
reviews the risk management policy on a periodic basis. 
Further, adequacy of design and operating effectiveness of key 
processes and controls, as documented in the risk and control 
matrices, are tested and a consolidated dashboard of Risk 
and Control review results across the Company and its key 
operating subsidiaries are presented to the GRMC and Audit 
& Governance Committee of the Board on a quarterly basis.
Further, to enable oversight of the Risk management function 
prevalent at each of the key operating subsidiaries, the 
management team of each key operating subsidiaries make 
presentation on key risk types, as defined in the respective 
Risk Management Policy, to the GRMC of the Company on a 
quarterly basis.
Financial reporting and fraud risks are duly considered in the 
risk management framework. Risks are mapped with controls 
and Risk management framework is revisited and revised 
based on prevailing practice and relevance.
Therefore, the Company has implemented a formal risk 
management policy and framework to ensure that a 
comprehensive risk management process is in place at all 
times, including appropriate board and senior management 
oversight and the process take into account appropriate 
steps to comply with applicable regulatory rules, regulations, 
principles and guidelines and to ensure the adequacy of 
relevant risk reporting to the Committees and Board.S.

INTERNAL FINANCIAL CONTROLS AND INTERNAL 
CONTROL SYSTEM
The Company and its subsidiaries have Internal Control 
Systems, commensurate with the size, scale and complexity 
of its operations, which encompasses the policies, standard 
operating procedures, approval/authorization matrix, circulars/ 
guidelines, and risk & control matrices for ensuring the orderly 
and efficient conduct of its business & support functions, 
adherence to these policies & procedures, the safeguarding 
of its assets, the prevention and detection of frauds and errors, 
the accuracy and completeness of the accounting records and 
timely preparation of reliable financial information during the 
process of financial reporting. Such detailed controls ensure 
productive and effective use of resources to the extent that 
the assets are safe-guarded, transactions are duly approved, 
registered and adequately reported and checks and balances 
ensure consistency and reliability of the accounting data.
Being a registered NBFC (CIC), the Company is exposed 
to various risks as stated in the Risk Management Policies 
of the Company and its subsidiaries. The Company and 
its subsidiaries have adequate control environment for 
identification, assessment, monitoring, mitigation and 
reporting of applicable risks on a periodical basis through 
an effective Risk Management Framework that has been 
developed encompassing all the key business and support 
functions. Mitigation plans and controls are documented for 
each identified risk in the form of policies & standard operating 
procedures and Risk & Control Matrices (RCM). Risks/controls 
documented in the RCMs are mapped to each of the financial 
statement line items (FSLI) and financial assertions to ensure 
comprehensiveness of the internal financial controls and 
mitigation plans. The Company has separate RCMs for Process 
Level Controls (PLC) and Entity Level Controls (ELC). Similarly, 
Information Technology controls relating to Information 
Security, Cyber Security and Other Information Technology General Controls (ITGC) have also been identified, assessed 
and documented, which are updated periodically.
Further, the Company and its subsidiaries have established 
robust framework for reviewing and strengthening the 
systems, policies, processes and procedures in order to 
mitigate the risks arising from time to time. Internal Financial 
Controls (IFC) documentation, including Standard Operating 
Procedures (SOPs) and Risk Control Matrices (RCMs), are 
reviewed and updated periodically to provide reasonable 
assurance regarding the effectiveness of internal controls. The 
management ensures that adequate controls are designed 
and operating effectively and that any control deficiencies 
identified during periodic reviews are addressed through 
timely corrective actions. The outcome of these periodic 
reviews including significant observations and the status of 
remediation measures, is reported to the Management and 
respective Committees of the Board on a quarterly basis.
The Company and its subsidiaries have an elaborate internal 
audit policy and framework approved by the respective Audit 
& Governance Committees of the Board. The scope, authority 
and structure of the Internal Audit function has been defined 
in the comprehensive Internal Audit Policy. The Company also 
conducts Information System and Cyber Security Audit on 
a yearly basis and the report is presented to the Audit and 
Governance Committee of the Board. Information System and 
Cyber Security Audit enable the Company to keep a check on 
technology-related risks and also improve business efficiency 
and distribution capabilities.
Based on the integrated report of internal audit and IFC, 
process owners undertake corrective action in their respective 
areas and thereby strengthen the internal controls. Significant 
internal audit observations (rated high and medium risk) and 
corrective actions thereon, along with IFC dashboard, are 
presented to the Audit and Governance Committee of the 
Board on periodical basis. The Internal Audit also assesses 
opportunities for improvement in business processes, systems 
and controls, provides recommendations, designed to add 
value to the organization and follow up the implementation of 
corrective actions. The Audit and Governance Committee of 
the Board reviews and evaluates adequacy and effectiveness 
of the Company’s internal control environment, provides their 
inputs, if any, to improve the quality of audit and assurance 
standards and monitors the implementation of audit 
recommendations across the relevant functional areas to 
continuously strengthen the internal control framework.
Therefore, the Board has laid down Internal Financial Controls 
to be followed by the Company and such internal Financial 
Controls are adequate and operating effectively during the 
financial year.CONFIRMATION UNDER FOREIGN EXCHANGE

Management Discussion and Analysis
Global Economy 
The global economy remained resilient through much of 
2025, supported by moderating inflation, easing financial 
conditions and sustained consumer spending across major 
economies. Global growth remained broadly steady despite 
persistent trade and geopolitical uncertainties, with continued 
investment in technology and services providing support 
to economic activity. However, the global outlook became 
increasingly uneven, as the year progressed, with differences 
in policy space, trade exposures and sensitivity to commodity 
prices shaping the pace of recovery across economies. 
During the second half of 2025, heightened trade tensions 
and protectionist measures, including higher tariffs by major 
economies, weighed on business confidence and cross-border 
investment, while continued realignment of global supply 
chains contributed to increased volatility across financial 
markets. Although, inflationary pressures had moderated 
across several economies, the pace of disinflation became 
less uniform, limiting the scope for an accelerated easing of 
monetary policy. 
The global environment  became more challenging in early 2026 
as geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and the resulting 
disruption in energy markets led to renewed volatility in crude 
oil prices and inflation expectations. The IMF's outlook projects 
global growth at 3.0% in 2026 and 3.4% in 2027, while noting 
that the energy shocks from the conflict is being partly offset 
by continued technology-led investment. Financial institutions 
prioritised prudent risk management, capital discipline and 
liquidity amid heightened uncertainties.  
Indian Economy 
India continued to be among the world’s fastest growing 
major economies during FY25-26, demonstrating resilience 
amid an increasingly uncertain global environment. Real GDP 
growth accelerated to 7.7%, supported by robust domestic 
consumption, sustained capital expenditure, healthy 
private investment and resilient services sector activity. 
The moderation in inflation and supportive macroeconomic 
policies further strengthened domestic economic 
conditions and provided favourable backdrop for investment 
and consumption.
Inflation moderated significantly during the year, with headline 
Consumer Price Index (CPI) inflation averaging around 4% and 
easing to 1.7% during the second half of calendar year. As price 
pressures receded, the Reserve Bank of India maintained a 
balanced monetary policy stance and kept the repo rate 
unchanged at 5.25%, supporting financial stability while 
ensuring adequate liquidity for productive sectors of the economy. Fiscal discipline also remained a priority, with the 
Government adhering to its fiscal consolidation roadmap and 
achieving a fiscal deficit of 4.4% of GDP, while sustaining capital 
expenditure of H11.21 Lakh Crore to strengthen infrastructure 
and long term economic competitiveness. 
Domestic demand remained the principal driver of growth, 
supported by improving rural conditions, moderating inflation, 
government-led infrastructure spending and sustained urban 
consumption.  Manufacturing activities continued to benefit 
from policy initiatives and investments, while the service sector 
remained a major contributor to economic activity, supported 
by technology-enabled services and Global Capabilities 
Centres.  The strength of domestic fundamentals was also 
reflected in the financial sector, with continued growth in 
bank credit, improving asset quality and resilient capital and 
liquidity positions. These conditions provided a supportive 
operating environment for financial institutions, evolving global 
trade dynamics, geopolitical uncertainties and commodity –
price volatility continued to warrant a calibrated approach to 
risk management, capital allocation and portfolio quality.
Industry Overview
The Non-Banking Financial Company sector continued 
to remain an important pillar of India’s Financial system, 
supporting credit growth across retail, MSME, vehicle finance, 
housing, consumer and other underserved segments. 
During FY25-26, the sector witnessed healthy credit growth, 
supported by resilient domestic economic activity, increasing 
formalisation and sustained demand for retail and business 
credit. The easing interest rate environment and improving 
liquidity conditions also supported funding costs, while 
lenders remained focused on prudent underwriting and 
asset quality, particularly across unsecured consumer credit 
and microfinance.
The sector continued to witness increasing adoption of 
technology, data analytics and digital lending platform, 
enabling NBFCs to improve customer acquisition, credit 
assessment, collections and operating efficiency. At the same 
time, competition from banks, fin-techs remained intense, 
increasing the focus on differentiated products, diversified 
funding, strong capitalisation and risk-adjusted returns.
Going forward, the outlook for the NBFC sector remains 
positive supported by India’s structural credit demand, rising 
consumption, financial inclusion and continued economic 
formalisation with sustainable growth dependent on 
maintaining asset quality, managing funding costs, leveraging 
technology and adhering to regulatory requirements. Health Insurance Business
India’s insurance sector has witnessed significant growth driven 
by increased awareness, favourable regulatory changes and 
greater participation from the private sector. Health insurance 
continued to maintain stronghold as the largest segment 
in India’s non-life insurance industry in FY26, with 44.3% 
share versus 41.4% in FY25. The health insurance segment 
grew 16.7% to about H 1.5 Lakh Crore, outpacing the overall  
non-life industry growth of 9.3% which stood at nearly  
H3.4 Lakh Crore during the year. Standalone health insurers 
contributed 30.8% of the total health insurance premium, 
underwriting H 45,866 Crore.
Health insurance reported the fastest growth among major 
non-life segments, primarily driven by strong traction in 
retail health policies following the GST rate reduction. Of the 
total health insurance premium, retail health insurance grew 
19.9% to H56,696 Crore, while group insurance rose 12.9% to 
H68,641 Crore. Retail health insurance has maintained strong 
momentum, with average growth in the range of 30–32% after 
the government exempted individual health policies, including 
family floaters and senior citizen covers, from GST, effective 
September 22, 2025. Resultantly, the share of retail in total 
health premiums increased to 38.1% from 37.1% in FY25, while 
group health insurance’s contribution declined to 46.1% from 
47.7% a year ago.
India’s insurance sector has deepened significantly in size and 
financial strength.
Financial Service Business
Retail Broking 
India’s equity markets witnessed a mixed operating 
environment in FY26, with heightened market volatility and 
weaker equity market performance impacting trading activity 
and investor sentiment. The Sensex and Nifty declines 7.1% 
and 5.1% respectively during the year, amid geopolitical 
uncertainties, foreign portfolio outflows and concerns around 
the global trade and tariffs. FPIs recorded net equity outflows 
of approximately $20.9 Billion during the year, while DIIs 
remained key source of market support with record purchases 
of around H 8.5 Lakh Crore.  
Despite the challenging market environment, retail 
participation continued to deepen, supported by digital 
adoption, financialisation of household savings and greater 
investor awareness. Approximately 3.2 crore new active demat 
accounts were added during the financial year, taking the 
total to over 22.5 crore, although additions moderated from  
4.1 crore in FY25. The primary market remained strong, with 
112 IPOs raising approximately H1.8 Lakh Crore, although 
average listing gains moderated to 8% from 30% in the previous 
year. Average daily turnover in the cash segment declined 
6% to H1.13 Lakh Crore while equity derivatives activity 
remained stable.The industry in increasingly transitioning from a traditional 
transaction-led broking model towards technology-enabled, 
diversified financial platforms, with brokers expanding into 
margin funding, wealth management, mutual fund distribution 
and other investment products. At the same time, regulatory 
measures aimed at curbing excessive retail participation 
in derivatives have influenced trading behaviour; options 
contract volumes declined materially in FY26 following 
tighter regulatory measures. Going forward, sustained retail 
participation, increasing penetration of digital investing and 
financialisation of savings are expected to support long-term 
growth of the sector, while competitive pricing, regulatory 
compliance, technology investments and the ability to 
diversify revenue streams beyond transaction based broking 
will remain key differentiator. 
MSME Lending 
The MSME sector continues to be a key contributor to India’s 
economic growth, employment and exports supported by 
increasing formalisation, digitalisation and improving access to 
institutional credit. The MSME credit ecosystem continued to 
expand during the financial year, with outstanding commercial 
credit balances reaching H 65.8 lakh Crore at March 2026, while 
entities with aggregate exposure above H 10 Lakh recorded 
healthy growth. New-to-credit (NTC) originations, however 
moderated, with their share declining from 52% in FY23 to 
42% in FY26, indicating increasing penetration of formal credit 
among established borrowers.   
NBFCs continue to play an important role in addressing the 
financing needs of MSMEs through customised products, 
faster credit assessment and wider reach, particularly in 
underserved segments. Growth is expected to remain healthy 
across secured MSME and loan-against-property segments, 
although lenders are maintaining a calibrated approach 
towards smaller-ticket and unsecured business loans amid 
elevated borrower leverages and emerging delinquencies. 
The outlook for MSME lending remains positive, supported 
by sustained credit demand and policy initiatives, while 
asset quality, prudent underwriting, technology-led credit 
assessment and effective collections will remain key to 
achieving sustainable growth.  
Housing Finance 
The affordable housing finance sector continues to play 
an important role in expanding home ownerships and 
financial inclusion, particularly among low and middle 
income household. Rising incomes, increasing urbanisation, 
nuclearisation of families and greater formalisation of the 
economy are supporting the demand for affordable housing. 
Despite the expansion of formal credit, a significant segment 
of self-employed and informal income borrowers, particularly 
in Tier II, Tier III and semi urban markets, remain underserved 
by the traditional lenders, creating structural opportunity for 
specialised affordable housing finance companies.

underwriting and collections. The segment is also benefitting 
from policy support, including the expansion of housing loans 
eligible under Priority Sector Lending Framework. However, 
lenders continue to remain focused on prudent underwriting 
and asset quality, particularly given the self-employed and 
informal income profile of a significant portion of the borrower 
base.

Performance
Care Health Insurance Limited

SAHI's. With a strong network of 277 branches, 4,10,000+ 
agents, ~22,040 hospital tie-ups across 1,455+ network 
locations, CHIL commands a premium position in the SAHI 
market. CHIL operates across three segments – personal 
accident insurance, health insurance and travel insurance. 
CHIL offers a diverse product portfolio of over 44 products, 
including group, travel, fixed benefit and indemnity categories, 
catering to various customer needs. Employing a multi-channel 
distribution strategy through agencies, brokers, corporate 
agents, online platforms and bancassurance, CHIL primarily 
focuses on retail and SME customers. It continues to invest in 
digital solutions for its customers, partners and employees.

Opportunities
The Indian health insurance market is growing, registering 
a market size of H1,48,748.20 Crore in FY26, an increase of 
16.71% from the previous year. Among health insurance service 
providers in India, public sector institutions hold a market 
share of 35.04%, private insurers have a 34.13% market share, 
and SAHI accounts for 30.83% of the market. However, in terms 
of retail GDP, SAHI held the largest share at 59.05% in FY26. 
Having invested in people, processes, alliances, technology, 
and customer service, CHIL is well-positioned to serve and 
grow within the structural growth narrative of the insurance 
sector in India, particularly in the health Insurance sector.
Threats
The continuous rise in healthcare costs is pressuring the 
health insurance business. Higher costs for medicines, 
advanced treatments, surgeries and hospital services are 
increasing medical inflation and average claim costs, which 
affects profitability. The impact may be greater during smaller cities. The continued shift towards formal credit, 
improving digital infrastructure and greater financial inclusion 
is expected to further expand the addressable market. For 
lenders, sustainable growth will depend on maintaining asset 
quality, efficient cost structures, diversified funding sources 
and strong customer acquisition and servicing capabilities, 
while maintaining growth with risk-adjusted returns. 
Business Overview 
About REL 
Religare Enterprises Limited (“REL” or “the Company”), a Core 
Investment Company (CIC), is a leading diversified financial 
services group offering an integrated suite of Financial Services 
and Health Insurance through its underlying subsidiaries and 
operating entities. It is registered with the Reserve Bank of India 
(RBI). 
Key Strategic Initiatives 
• Preferential Issue
  During FY26, the Company achieved a significant 
milestone in strengthening its capital base through the 
implementation of preferential issue of convertible 
warrants approved by the shareholders in the
